candidates.name: forge-task-implementation
candidates.description: How to execute one RepoSignal forge-task contract end to end: read the task block, honour its exclusions and constraints, produce the named outputs, run the named validation commands, and stop at the human review gate instead of self-serving it.
candidates.reason: The package at .opencode/skills/forge-task-implementation already covers this process and still matches the source: all 40 implementation tasks across the 11 feature documents share one contract shape, three tasks modify the same three files by design, and the exclusion column is the hard boundary a task-by-task agent overruns first. It keeps the reading order, the validate-before-reporting rule and the refusal to author a human gate, and it claims nothing the task blocks do not require. No gap was found in it while re-reading the task blocks against the agents, so reuse it unchanged rather than regenerating it.

candidates.name: honest-data-rendering
candidates.description: The no-fabrication rules for every RepoSignal layer that reads, computes or renders the archive: a missing day stays a gap, insufficient data is a first-class result, absolute values precede percentages, backfilled and collected days are labelled apart, and no output carries a score, threshold, verdict or unsupported directional claim.
candidates.reason: This is the product's central invariant under RS-DU-02 and RS-HO-01, it has the widest blast radius in the team, and each failure of it looks like working code - a zero substituted for a gap, a bridged polyline, an interpolated delta, a verdict word. It is also the most repeated requirement in the feature set, re-asserted in acceptance criteria across storage, backfill, collection, insight, chart, page data and views. The existing package states each rule once with the assertion that proves it, and its consumer list matches the seven agents whose surfaces can violate it, so reuse it as written.

candidates.name: token-and-egress-safety
candidates.description: RepoSignal credential and outbound-request safety: the 0600 credential file, redaction of token-shaped values from every error and log surface, the api.github.com allowlist enforced before a socket opens, GET-only requests with no request body, and the REPO_SIGNAL_ALLOW_LOCAL_TRANSPORT test-override gate that test suites and stubs depend on.
candidates.reason: RS-SC-01, RS-SC-02, RS-SC-04, RS-SP-03, RS-SP-04 and RS-SP-05 form one coupled boundary: the same token is read by the credential store, resolved through the provider interface, attached by the transport, and must never reach a log, an error, a row, a page or a test snapshot. The local transport override is the single most reused fragile mechanism in the plan, appearing in the collect, discover, collection e2e, server e2e and dashboard e2e suites, and its gate is what keeps the outbound allowlist guarantee mechanical rather than asserted. The package documents the five suites that set it, the redaction surfaces and the proof that the refusal happens with the flag absent; it is accurate and complete against the source, so reuse it.

candidates.name: github-rest-contract
candidates.description: The pinned GitHub REST contract RepoSignal depends on: the 2026-03-10 API version constant and its header set, the 14-day traffic window bound, 202 Accepted as retryable only for statistics endpoints, the stargazer star-timestamp media type with last-page pagination, the typed error taxonomy, and the vendor documentation pages that must be re-read rather than remembered.
candidates.reason: PRD section 6.4 lists the vendor pages the product depends on and section 16 fixes the recorded defaults for both the API version and the fine-grained permission, which makes this the plan's main external drift surface - GitHub can change a payload, a media type or a status code, and the PRD already names a live human re-check gate as the mitigation. The client owner, the collector that must survive a 202, the discover command and the three suites that mock the service all need the same assumptions recorded once rather than restated per module. The package's page-by-page reference table and typed error taxonomy match the feature documents without drift, so reuse it and leave the version constant where it is.

candidates.name: archive-storage-discipline
candidates.description: Writing and migrating the RepoSignal SQLite archive safely: the node:sqlite connection settings including the enableDefensive guard that sets the engine floor, forward-only migrations recorded with content checksums, last-write-wins day-series upsert carrying source and collection timestamp, append-only snapshot captures, one transaction per repository, no code path that deletes a fact row, and calendarDays for telling a stored zero from a missing day.
candidates.reason: The package is correct on everything except the runtime floor, and the PRD revision of 2026-09-30 invalidated that one statement: it now says the engine floor is the release where node:sqlite dropped the --experimental-sqlite flag, while PRD 6.1 and 16 fix the floor at the release exposing enableDefensive and telemetry-storage RS-DB-01 records the same prerequisite. Extend it additively with the enableDefensive requirement, the rule that a PRAGMA is not a substitute for SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE, the fail-closed behaviour when the runtime lacks the API, and a gotcha for the misleading import-succeeds-then-connection-fails symptom. Keep every existing step, the per-table write rules and the consumer list unchanged; the correction is guidance on top of the package, not a replacement for it.

candidates.name: cli-command-surface
candidates.description: Adding and testing a RepoSignal subcommand: register it in src/commands/index.js, honour the 0 success / 1 operational failure / 2 usage error exit-code contract, print usage for --help and for an unknown command, emit one fact per line with no credential material, support the dry-run and filter flags the command plan names, and prove reachability by spawning node src/cli.js.
candidates.reason: Five features add commands to one shared registry with one shared exit-code and output contract - config init and check, db migrate/status/verify/backup/restore, discover, collect and serve - and each task's acceptance criteria assert reachability through the process entry point rather than an import, a convention that is easy to get wrong in a way that passes locally. The package's command inventory, exit-code mapping and spawn-not-import rule match all five feature documents, and the registry contract stays with platform-engineer while the bodies stay with each owner. Nothing in the PRD revision touches this surface, so reuse it unchanged.

candidates.name: accessible-server-rendered-views
candidates.description: Building RepoSignal's server-rendered pages and SVG chart to WCAG 2.1 AA: one escaping helper per context, the shared document shell, exactly one main landmark, a skip link first in the tab order, unbroken heading order, a data table paired with every figure, text-first states, and colour tokens declared once with contrast ratios computed by a test.
candidates.reason: RS-AX-01 through RS-AX-07 apply to the router's escaping helpers, the shell, the three view modules, the SVG chart and the stylesheet, so the same structural assertions would otherwise be re-derived in the router, html, chart, view and integration tasks. The existing implement-visual-theme package cannot be reused for this and must not be extended: it is bound to a React DOM and PixiJS renderer stack and a different design system, whereas this product has no client-side framework, no charting library and system fonts only, so extending it would import foreign assumptions. The project package already states the per-context helpers, the structural assertions and the computed contrast rule against this product's own file layout, so reuse it.

candidates.name: verification-loop
candidates.description: The RepoSignal verification loop: run tests through scripts/run-tests.mjs so a zero-test selection fails, type-check with tsc --noEmit over checkJs JSDoc types, mirror the source layout under tests/, give every run a temporary REPO_SIGNAL_HOME, and drive entry-point tests by spawning node src/cli.js rather than importing a module.
candidates.reason: Every task names two validation commands drawn from this loop, and RS-TC-04 makes a command that proves nothing an unacceptable check, so the loop's shape is load-bearing in the tasks, the CI workflow and the release checklist. Its structure is right, but the same PRD revision that moved the engine floor invalidates two statements: the SKILL.md gotcha and one row of the failure-recovery table both say a host below Node 22.13 fails on a missing experimental flag, when the binding constraint is now enableDefensive and the observed symptom is a connection-time API-drift error rather than an import error. Extend it additively with the corrected floor, the corrected symptom and its fix, and a new table row for the drift error; keep the wrapper rule, the type-check step, the mirroring convention, the temporary-home rule and the spawn-not-import rule unchanged.

candidates.name: documentation-contract-tests
candidates.description: Writing RepoSignal's operator and public documents so they stay true, with the test that fails when they drift: every command named in a runbook must exist in the repository, the README must retain its no-fabrication, redistribution, permission and Node-range statements, the CI workflow must run install, typecheck and the fail-on-empty test wrapper, and no document may state a test result or approval that was not observed.
candidates.reason: Four consecutive operations tasks build the same fragile artefact - a document plus a test that fails when the document drifts - and RS-OPS-CON-01 forbids stating an unobserved result or approval. The failure mode is specific and expensive: a runbook documenting a command that does not exist, or a README that quietly loses the statement that GitHub's traffic data may not be redistributed, and the automated checks pass either way unless a test asserts the sentence. One consumer owns all four tasks, but the procedure recurs four times and the documents outlive the code they describe. Its Node-range and two-version assertions are written as the supported floor rather than a fixed number, so the PRD revision does not invalidate them; reuse it unchanged.

candidates.name: human-review-gate-protocol
candidates.description: How agents treat the six human review gates (foundation security, legibility spike, dashboard accessibility, live GitHub integration, seven-day soak, open-source posture) without authoring, editing or self-certifying them.
candidates.reason: The responsibility is real but it is already carried by the artifact that would describe it: every gate is a forge-task with no model owner, a reviewFile path, and an explicit constraint that no agent may author or complete it, and each adjacent agent states the prohibition locally in its own Human Gates section naming its own gates. Eight of the nine specialists name at least one gate that way - platform-engineer RS-FND-REV-01 and RS-OPS-REV-01, github-integration-engineer and cli-engineer RS-OPS-LIVE-01, collector-engineer RS-OPS-SOAK-01, insight-engineer RS-VIZ-REV-01, ui-engineer RS-VIZ-REV-01 and RS-UI-REV-01, server-engineer RS-OPS-LIVE-01 and RS-UI-REV-01, qa-engineer RS-OPS-LIVE-01, RS-OPS-SOAK-01 and RS-UI-REV-01 - leaving only data-engineer, whose feature carries no review task. A shared package would add a second place to maintain the same prohibition and would make self-certification easier to reach for rather than harder. The correct home is the task contract, which is immutable input.

candidates.name: node-sqlite-upgrade-drill
candidates.description: Re-verifying the storage layer after a Node major upgrade, given that node:sqlite is a release candidate and the engine range is pinned to one LTS line.
candidates.reason: This is a single future event, not a repeated process: PRD 12.2 names it as a risk and PRD 16 fixes the engine range, and the release checklist already carries the schema version and the supported Node range a re-check would use. The 2026-09-30 floor revision also shows the mechanism that matters - the storage layer detects the missing API and fails closed rather than degrading - which is guidance for the existing archive-storage-discipline package rather than a new occasion. When the upgrade is actually planned, the backup drill, the migration runner's checksum behaviour and the existing suite already exercise the surface that matters, so a dedicated package would be scaffolding for an occasion that has not occurred.
